subject: Approval request: early termination & ramp addendum for Novus Health pilot
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@novushealth.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Early termination & ramp protection for pilot

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Novus is excited to move forward with a 6-month pilot, but procurement has pushed back on a couple of contract items that we'd like your help resolving quickly so we can avoid a procurement delay.

Key asks from our side:
- Early termination clause with a downsell protection: if Novus reduces commitment after month 3, we want a capped refund/exit amount and a 3-month ramp schedule so our users aren't cut off abruptly.
- Opt-out language for the pilot that allows Novus to step down to a smaller footprint with predictable pricing so we can test in a single region.

We attached a short addendum that outlines the language we prefer (Doc attached to this message). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a capped early termination equal to 3 months of committed spend and a ramp of 50%/75%/100% over three months? Procurement is aiming to sign by next Tuesday.

Appreciate a quick reply — cc'ing our procurement lead Tim Jones (procurement@novushealth.com).

Best,
Sarah

Novus Health

Marissa, Karthik, Laura —

Looping you in on an ask from Novus Health (details below). They want a pilot addendum with: a) early termination capped at 3 months committed spend, b) a 3-month ramp-down schedule (50%/75%/100%), and c) explicit opt-out language to allow scaling down to a smaller footprint mid-pilot. Procurement wants sign-off by next Tue (7/6).

My read: this is a high-velocity pilot, strategic for our healthcare vertical. I don't want legal to slow this down, but we need clarity on the financial impact and an approved concession guideline for Deal Desk.

Ask: can I get executive approval (or a concrete counter) on the concession and opt-out language? Proposed commercial terms for Deal Desk signoff:
- One-time concession cap: 15% of committed ARR (applied as a credit over 3 months) OR capped at 3 months committed spend (whichever is smaller).
- Ramp schedule: 50% month 1, 75% month 2, 100% month 3 (for service continuity).
- Opt-out: Novus can downscale to a single-region footprint with a 30-day notice; any permanent reduction requires a signed amendment and 30-day lead.

Attached: Novus_Ramp_Addendum_v1.docx (their proposed language).

If legal/finance are OK, I'll send a counter and aim to get a DocuSign amendment ready ASAP.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — I reviewed Novus's addendum and sketched inline edits. High-level legal guidance:

- Early termination cap: the 3-month cap is reasonable from a customer experience standpoint. We should convert "months of committed spend" into a defined monetary cap tied to the "Committed Monthly Revenue (CMR)" in the SOW to avoid ambiguity.
- Ramp language: their 50%/75%/100% schedule is fine, but we need a clause that prevents immediate reuse of reserved capacity to avoid double-counting. Add a sentence: "Reserved capacity released as part of the ramp may not be allocated to replacement workloads for 30 days."
- Opt-out: prefer a 30-day notice for short-term downscales and require a signed amendment for permanent reductions. For pilots, require the amendment to be signed within 10 business days of notifying Redwood, or full rates resume.

I can accept the 15% concession cap if Finance signs off on the math and we codify the cap as a dollar amount in the amendment. Please advise if we should route to the Exec Review Committee for anything beyond 15%.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Team — quick finance read:

- A 15% concession cap sounds acceptable provided it's applied as a credit over the three-month ramp and we document the dollar cap tied to committed MRR.
- Financial impact (rough): Novus pilot is $60k/mo committed for 6 months (projected). 15% concession = $54k total cap (spread ~ $18k/mo over the three-month ramp).
- Condition: require the pilot amendment signed within 10 business days, and require minimum retained MRR of 40% in month 1 of ramp to avoid additional clawbacks.

I'm attaching a short worksheet showing the scenario math. If marketing/sales want to increase the concession, route to RevOps for a modeled counter.

Laura Bennett

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Approval: Novus Health pilot ramp & early termination (conditional)

Thanks for the good write-ups. I approve the proposed approach with the following conditions (so Deal Desk has clear guardrails):

1) Commercial concession: approve up to 15% of committed ARR as a cap — convert to a dollar cap in the amendment. No further executive escalation needed for concessions <= 15%.
2) Early termination: cap at 3 months of committed spend (expressed as the dollar cap above).
3) Ramp schedule: accept 50% month 1, 75% month 2, 100% month 3. Require clause preventing reuse of reserved capacity for 30 days.
4) Opt-out/process: Novus must sign the amendment within 10 business days of counter; require 30-day notice for permanent downscales. If the amendment is not executed in 10 business days, standard rates apply and concession is void.
5) Finance condition: maintain minimum 40% retained MRR in month 1 of the ramp, otherwise Redwood may reclaim credits or accelerate payments.

Action: Dylan — please prepare the counter with Marissa's redlines and the dollar cap from Laura's worksheet, send to Novus, and initiate DocuSign (link in metadata) aiming for signature by Tue 7/6. If procurement pushes additional demands, escalate to me immediately.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
